answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample and slash the stake when linked accounts submit coordinated fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the attacker’s capital: every account must tie up funds, and detected cheating destroys them. The rule should reward verified outcomes, not account count, so a voyage, a quartz shipment, or a fable-writing task cannot be farmed simply by minting identities.
